claims.statement: Carrier Operations confirms that corrections to pickup slots are reversible and must run only after the affected feed's lag is identified and corrected
claims.corroboration: Tier-1 verified response from Carrier Operations confirming procedure
claims.limitation: Does not directly state whether a lag exists on the east-node feed or whether carrier has slots on file; only confirms that corrections are reversible

capability_gaps.reason: Need to understand the specific changes in v18 that affect split-reservation logic and east-node priority; this will clarify whether the allocation rule itself is defective or functioning as designed but creating an unintended interaction with the carrier pickup process

next_action.rationale: We have two plausible mechanisms: (1) v18 allocation logic is defective, causing split-reservation that prevents valid pickup, or (2) v18 is working correctly but interacts with a carrier feed lag. Reviewing the rule change history will clarify the intent and implementation of v18's east-node priority logic, discriminating between these hypotheses.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Understanding what v18 changed will reveal whether the split-reservation is an intended side effect or a defect, and whether it could prevent carrier pickup integration
